'''Elections to [[Isle of Wight Council]]''' took place on 6 May 2021 as part of the [[2021 United Kingdom local elections]]. These were held at the same time as the [[2021 England and Wales police and crime commissioner elections|elections]] for the [[Hampshire Police and Crime Commissioner]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Elections Management - Service Details|url=https://www.iow.gov.uk/Council/Elections/Elections-Management/PCC-and-Local-Elections-May-2021|access-date=2021-04-05|website=www.iow.gov.uk}}</ref> The elections saw the Conservatives lose control of the council, losing seats against the national trend for the party.

== Background ==
New ward divisions were used for this election, with thirty wards changing,<ref>{{Cite web|title=What will the Isle of Wight be voting for on May 6? Election explained|url=https://www.countypress.co.uk/news/politics/19087022.may-6-election-explained-isle-wight-voters/|access-date=2021-04-05|website=Isle of Wight County Press|language=en}}</ref> with the number of wards reduced by one to 39 single-member seats.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Local Government Boundary Commission for England Consultation Portal|url=https://consultation.lgbce.org.uk/node/12655|access-date=2021-04-05|website=consultation.lgbce.org.uk|archive-date=2021-03-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210326002334/https://consultation.lgbce.org.uk/node/12655|url-status=dead}}</ref> In the previous election, the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] had won a majority with twenty five seats, with [[Independent politician|Independents]] (including the [[Island Independents|Island Independent Group]]), [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]], [[Green Party of England and Wales|Greens]], and [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] also winning seats.

For the 2021 election, as well as existing independent candidates, the new Our Island also announced its intention to support several independent candidates.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-02-01|title=Our Island announce their first candidates for May 2021 Isle of Wight council elections|url=https://onthewight.com/our-island-announce-their-first-candidates-for-may-2021-isle-of-wight-council-elections/|access-date=2021-04-05|website=Isle of Wight News from OnTheWight|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Our Island Archives|url=https://onthewight.com/about/our-island/|access-date=2021-04-05|website=Isle of Wight News from OnTheWight|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Toogood|first=Darren|date=2021-02-01|title=FIRST 'OUR ISLAND' ELECTION CANDIDATES ANNOUNCED|url=https://www.islandecho.co.uk/first-our-island-election-candidates-announced/|access-date=2021-04-05|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Aftermath ==
The incumbent Conservative leader of the council lost his seat to the Green Party,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countypress.co.uk/news/19287725.conservative-isle-wight-council-leader-dave-stewart-loses-seat/|title = Conservative Isle of Wight Council Leader loses seat to Green}}</ref> and was replaced as group leader by Steve Hastings, who subsequently invited other councillors to coalition talks.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countypress.co.uk/news/19290068.acting-tory-leader-invites-opposition-join-form-majority/|title = Acting Tory leader invites opposition councillors to join and form majority}}</ref>

On 26 May, independent councillor Lora Peacey-Wilcox was elected leader of the council with 20 votes to Hastings’s 18. There was a single abstention from the Labour councillor, who was absent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countypress.co.uk/news/19331240.council-conservative-boss-steve-hastings-promises-robust-opposition/|title = Conservatives promise 'robust' opposition as Team Alliance wins council control}}</ref> Island Independent Network councillor Ian Stephens was elected her deputy. Independent councillor Geoff Brodie was elected as the Chair of the Council, with Green councillor Claire Critchison elected Vice-Chair.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.islandecho.co.uk/lora-peacey-wilcox-elected-as-the-new-leader-of-the-isle-of-wight-council/|title = Lora Peacey-Wilcox Elected as the New Leader of the Isle of Wight Council|date = 26 May 2021}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-hampshire-57265230|title = Isle of Wight Council appoints Independent Lora Peacey-Wilcox as new leader|work = BBC News|date = 27 May 2021}}</ref>

The leadership and cabinet - termed the "Alliance Group" - includes Independent, Green, Island Independent Network and Our Island councillors who together make up 18 of the 39 seats on the council. With the additional external support from the Liberal Democrats and the Vectis Party this constitutes a majority of 20 out of the 39 council seats.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iowlibdems.org.uk/en/article/2021/1406576/isle-of-wight-council-under-new-leadership|title = Isle of Wight Council under new leadership}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-hampshire-57265230|title = Isle of Wight Council appoints Independent Lora Peacey-Wilcox as new leader|work = BBC News|date = 27 May 2021}}</ref>

In August 2021, Cllr Brodie quit the Alliance Group over planning issues, but continues to support the administration.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countypress.co.uk/news/19538593.isle-wight-council-leader-reassured-brodie-support-pledge/|title=Geoff Brodie resignation: Council leader pleased by promise of support}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.countypress.co.uk/news/19537554.isle-wight-council-chair-geoff-brodie-quits-ruling-alliance/|title = Council chair quits ruling Alliance Group}}</ref>

===Lake North===
A by-election was held in Lake North on 1 May 2025, triggered by the resignation of Conservative councillor Tig Outlaw. David Maclean was elected for Reform.

A by-election was held in Lake North on 2 October 2025, triggered by the resignation of Reform councillor David Maclean. Bill Nigh was elected for Reform.
